body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 46f4ca06266fa3d7a4679ac952252235e8134f6c -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- Safety floor holds. The PR touches no golden and no snapshot. Neither lathe post declares `explains`, and the new manifest globals are read only inside `explain()` and `form()`, which run only when Explain is on. So posted output with Explain off is unchanged for every shipped post, mill posts included. With no tables declared, `_explainCheck()` returns "" and `_explainWord` falls through to the old mill table.
- An explanation can only add a comment. `explain()` still goes through the existing guards (printable ASCII, delimiters, the active-keyword lead, the length cap). Folding `G50 S` into one meaning only affects the comment text, and the posted words are untouched. The new test also checks that each Explain-on line is its plain line plus one comment.
- No meaning is guessed. `G50` without `S` says nothing, `T0100` says "NO OFFSET", and any other T form on a station-offset post stays silent. A mill post keeps G99 as R-height and T101 as tool 101.
- A malformed table is refused by name, before any hook, and only when Explain is on.
- Provenance and the decision file are present. No `PROCESS_VERSION` bump is needed (only `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` changed, which is not a process file).

**Results** (locally, in my own worktree, merged with main; the runner was not used)
- `explain_lathe`: 3/3 pass on the PR.
- The same 3 tests with main's `explain.rs` and `js.rs` swapped in (the PR's posts kept): 3/3 FAIL, as claimed. I restored the PR's files afterwards.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: every suite green, including `explain`, `script_fanuc_lathe` and `script_tormach_lathe`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.

**Requested before merge:** none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The 60-character cap on fanuc-lathe's opening block will cut the G99 meaning once #1387 / #1388 wire `explains`. The PR body already says so.
- I did not run the app suites, the ui suites or the release-tier lanes.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
